|strategy=By Edward Tostanoski, Gold 3<ref name="decipher-strategy">https://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/specialedition/dark/small/oppressiveenforcement.html</ref>

Opressive Enforcement has may different effects on the game. Adding destiny +1 to your ISD's is nice, to your Victory-class SD's is good, and to your Dreadnoughts (giving them 4) is great. So its use in a space-drain deck is obvious.

The only Immediate Effects that benefit from being Free are the original ones, [[Tentacle]] and [[There'll Be Hell To Pay]], but that's okay. They're both great cards, cramping many styles, from SAC to [[Grimtaash]] to [[Nabrun Leids]] to Hyper-Escape to [[The Signal]] and [[Nar Shaddaa Wind Chimes]]. And it may be better than [[There Is No Try]] against [[Sense (Dark){{!}}Sense]] And [[Alter (Dark){{!}}Alter]], because while in both cases you may lose a crucial Interrupt or Effect tactically, as it goes Used, you know strategically it will be back, and for now a (usually) high destiny card is back in your Life Force.

Combos:

Opressive Enforcement + [[Twi'lek Advisor]]: As you only need one of these in play, you only need one in your Reserve Deck.

Opressive Enforcement + [[There'll Be Hell To Pay]] + [[Tentacle]]: Your Interrupt worries are over, while your opponent's have just begun. I hope he remembers how many [[Nar Shaddaa Wind Chimes]] he put in his deck.

Opressive Enforcement + Dreadnaughts: Destiny 4 support cards for your TIE decks.
